html:
The Tupian languages are a family of about seventy languages of South America. The best known are Tupi, once spoken along the coast of Brazil, and Guarani, today an official language of Paraguay.

Its largest branch, Tupi-Guarani, spread along rivers and down the Atlantic coast. When the Portuguese arrived around 1500, Tupi peoples such as the Tupinamba and Tupi held much of the coast. A simplified Tupi, the lingua geral, became the common speech of colonial Brazil, and Guarani was written and printed in the Jesuit reductions.

Other Tupian peoples live in the Amazon, such as the Munduruku, Sateré-Mawé, Yudjá and the Kawahib groups like the Parintintin. The Aché of Paraguay and the Ka'apor speak Tupi-Guarani languages too.
